title: Scaling Laws for Data Filtering—Data Curation cannot be Compute Agnostic
data_curation: Core focus. Uses the DataComp medium-scale pool of 128M image-caption pairs as the unfiltered base, then partitions it into quality buckets via two ranking metrics: CLIP score (image-caption similarity from a pretrained CLIP L/14) and T-MARS score (CLIP score after masking OCR text in images). LAION filtering retains ~10% with CLIP score > 0.28; T-MARS originally retains ~30%. Buckets are formed by score percentile (Top 10%, Top 10-20%, Top 20-30%, Top 30-40%), each ~12.8M samples. The central thesis is the quality-quantity tradeoff (QQT): high-quality subsets are small and lose utility when repeated, so the optimal filtering aggressiveness depends on total compute (32M, 64M, 128M, 640M samples seen). DataComp enforces NSFW filtering and face blurring. Scaling laws are also validated on Cherti et al. (2023) pretrained models spanning pool sizes 80M-2B and compute 3B-34B.
curriculum: Not a focus of this paper. There is no multi-stage post-training pipeline; the work studies single-stage contrastive CLIP pretraining for 2-10 epochs on individual score-ranked pools (and up to 30-40 epochs in CLIP generally). The only 'ordering' is a compute-adaptive selection rule: train on the highest-quality bucket alone at low compute (fewer repetitions), then progressively include lower-quality buckets (Top 10% -> Top 20% -> Top 30%) as compute grows, to avoid the diminishing utility of repeated high-quality data.
method: Introduces scaling laws for heterogeneous, limited web data that extend y = a*n^b + d. Two additions: (1) utility decays exponentially with repetition, b_{k+1} = b*(1/2)^(k/tau) = b*delta^k, with half-life tau capturing pool diversity, giving a closed-form loss y_k = a*n_1^{b_1} * prod_{j=2}^k (n_j/n_{j-1})^{b_j} + d; (2) Theorem 1 combines p pools without jointly training on them: the merged repetition half-life becomes tau_hat = p*tau and the effective utility b_eff is a weighted mean of per-pool utilities. For contrastive CLIP, where a pool of N samples yields O(N^2) comparisons, tau scales with pool size: tau_hat = (N_hat/N)*tau. Parameters (utility b, half-life tau, shared normalizer a, irreducible d) are fit by grid search, since gradient/SciPy optimizers were unstable. Three axiom formulations are compared; only the utility-decay version handles heterogeneous mixtures.
eval_metrics: Evaluates zero-shot on ImageNet-1k and average accuracy over 18 DataComp tasks: ImageNet plus six ImageNet-OOD variants (V2, R, A, Sketch, O, ObjectNet), six VTAB datasets (Caltech-101, CIFAR10/100, Flowers102, Pets, RESISC45), Food-101, Pascal VOC 2007, Stanford Cars, and MSCOCO/Flickr retrieval. Metrics: top-1 accuracy, Mean per Class Recall (selected VTAB), and Mean Recall@1 (retrieval). Headline findings: at 128M samples seen, LAION filtering beats no-filtering by +7.5% avg accuracy over 18 tasks, but beyond ~450M samples unfiltered common crawl overtakes LAION-filtered data. The Pareto-optimal filtering shifts from Top 10% T-MARS at 32M compute to Top 20% at 100-350M and Top 30% beyond 350M. The scaling law also accurately predicts error for Cherti et al. ViT-B/16 and ViT-B/32 models trained at 3B-34B compute, where prior fits had large errors.
key_results: At 128M compute, LAION filtering gives +7.5% avg zero-shot accuracy over 18 tasks versus no-filtering, but beyond ~450M samples seen, unfiltered common crawl outperforms LAION-filtered data. The proposed scaling laws predict the Pareto-optimal filtering strategy across 32M-640M compute on the DataComp 128M pool (Top 10% best at 32M, Top 20% at 100-350M, Top 30% beyond 350M) and accurately extrapolate to Cherti et al. ViT-B/16 and ViT-B/32 models at 3B-34B compute.
evolution_note: Builds on Kaplan (2020) and Hoffmann/Chinchilla (2022) scaling laws and on Muennighoff et al. (2023)'s observation that >4 epochs yield negligible gains, but extends these to heterogeneous web data and contrastive CLIP training, where prior fits (Cherti et al. 2023) failed for repeated data. It reacts against compute-agnostic filtering practices (LAION, T-MARS, DFN) and motivates later compute-adaptive data curation for foundation-model pretraining.
